title: Systematic Error
notes:
Definition

The error which tends to occur in one direction, either positive or negative, is called systematic error.

Examples

  • Instrumental errors
  • Imperfection in experimental technique
  • Personal errors
  • Errors due to external cause
examples:
**Q1: Define systematic error.**

**Answer:** Error that tends to occur consistently in one direction (positive or negative).

**Q2: Name the four sources of systematic error.**

**Answer:** Instrumental errors, imperfection in experimental technique, personal errors, errors due to external cause.

**Q3: What causes instrumental errors?**

**Answer:** Imperfect design of the measuring instrument.

**Q4: Give the classic example of imperfection in experimental technique from the notes.**

**Answer:** A thermometer under the armpit gives a lower reading than actual body temperature.

**Q5: What causes personal errors?**

**Answer:** Inexperience of the observer, e.g., lack of proper apparatus setting.

**Q6: What external conditions cause systematic errors?**

**Answer:** Changes in temperature, pressure, humidity during the experiment.

**Q7: Is systematic error random in direction?**

**Answer:** No, it consistently occurs in one direction.

**Q8: Can systematic error be corrected?**

**Answer:** Yes, by calibration or correcting the technique/instrument.

**Q9: Give an example of an instrumental error.**

**Answer:** A weighing scale that always shows 100g extra due to a manufacturing defect.

**Q10: How is systematic error different from random error?**

**Answer:** Systematic error is consistent/directional; random error is irregular and unpredictable.

**Q11: Which subtype of systematic error relates to the observer's skill?**

**Answer:** Personal errors.

**Q12: Which subtype relates to environmental conditions?**

**Answer:** Errors due to external cause.

**Q13: Which subtype relates to flaws in the device itself?**

**Answer:** Instrumental errors.

**Q14: Which subtype relates to the method/procedure used?**

**Answer:** Imperfection in experimental technique.

**Q15: If a scale is always 1kg heavier due to a fault, what type of error is this?**

**Answer:** Systematic (instrumental) error.

**Q16: If humidity changes affect a reading consistently, what error type is this?**

**Answer:** Systematic error due to external cause.

**Q17: Can systematic errors be reduced by increasing the number of trials?**

**Answer:** No, unlike random error, averaging does not remove systematic error.

**Q18: What word describes the direction consistency of systematic error?**

**Answer:** One-directional (either always positive or always negative).

**Q19: Give a personal error example besides the one in the notes.**

**Answer:** Consistently misreading a scale due to parallax by an inexperienced observer.

**Q20: Why is a zero error in an instrument a systematic error?**

**Answer:** Because it shifts every reading in the same direction by a fixed amount.

**Q21: How can instrumental errors be minimized?**

**Answer:** By properly calibrating or servicing the instrument.

**Q22: How can personal errors be minimized?**

**Answer:** By training the observer and following correct procedure.

**Q23: How can errors due to external cause be minimized?**

**Answer:** By controlling the environment (temperature, pressure, humidity).

**Q24: Is body temperature measurement via armpit thermometer typically over or under actual value?**

**Answer:** Under (lower than actual body temperature).

**Q25: Name one real scenario combining two subtypes of systematic error.**

**Answer:** A poorly calibrated instrument (instrumental) used by an untrained observer (personal) in a hot room (external cause).
